Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure stems from ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int) not detecting that the underlying input stream has ended prematurely while inflating a DEFLATED entry. In the multi-volume archive used by the test, the last entry is truncated (first volume ends mid-entry). Here is how it unfolds:

1) The test reads entries using getNextEntry() until it reaches the truncated last entry and then starts reading its data in a loop:
   - while ((read = zi.read(buffer)) > 0) { }
   - It expects an IOException("Truncated ZIP file").

2) In ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int) (lines 191–246), the DEFLATED path is taken (current.getMethod() != STORED). The method relies on java.util.zip.Inflater inf:
   - If inf.needsInput() is true, fill() is called (lines 227–232).
   - fill() (lines 328–335) calls in.read(buf). When the archive is truncated mid-entry, in.read(buf) returns -1. fill() sets lengthOfLastRead to -1 and does not feed the Inflater (since it only calls inf.setInput if > 0).

3) After fill(), read() proceeds to call inf.inflate(buffer, start, length) (lines 233–238). With no more input available and the inflater not finished, inflate returns 0. The current code then:
   - Checks only if (read == 0 && inf.finished()) to return -1 (lines 239–241).
   - Otherwise, it returns read (0) (lines 242–243).

4) This results in read() returning 0 bytes instead of throwing or signaling EOF, exactly as reported in the bug: “All calls to read() will return 0 bytes read.” The test’s loop exits without an exception and then fails with “shouldn’t be able to read from truncated entry” because it expected an IOException with message "Truncated ZIP file".

5) The same underlying issue also affects subsequent entry handling. getNextEntry() (lines 107–185) first calls closeEntry() if current != null (line 112). closeEntry() calls skip(Long.MAX_VALUE) (lines 294–303), and skip repeatedly calls read(...) until -1 is encountered (lines 255–267). Because read() keeps returning 0 in the truncated case, skip() never progresses, potentially causing an infinite loop inside closeEntry() and preventing getNextEntry() from throwing an exception as the test expects.

In summary, the root cause is missing EOF/truncation detection in read() for DEFLATED entries: when the inflater needs input but the underlying stream has hit EOF (fill() saw in.read == -1), read() should not return 0. It should throw an IOException with the message "Truncated ZIP file". This change will both satisfy the test’s expectation for an exception during data read and ensure that a subsequent call to getNextEntry() also fails (via closeEntry/skip invoking read again and rethrowing).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
